Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

according to preposition

as someone says or reports

also according to him, according to her, as he says, as they say

classical

Gell. 1.18.2: nōn leporem dīcimus, ut ait
Varr. RR 2.5.3: ut scrībit Tīmaeus
Sen. Ep. 84.3: ut ajunt

ut ait

as he (she) says: according to (him, her)

With the name: ut ait Ennius; with a book, ut scrībit; for hearsay, ut ajunt, as they say.

Other words

  • auctor est — X is the authority for it, X reports (with accusative and infinitive)

    also used · classical · Tac. Ann. 13.20: Fabius Rūsticus auctor est (Lewis & Short); Plin. NH 11.73: auctōrēs sunt (Lewis & Short)

    The historians’ way of naming a source; see source (of information).

Examples

  • Graecia enim antīqua, ut scrībit Tīmaeus, taurōs vocābat italōs

    for in ancient Greece, according to Timaeus, bulls were called <em>italoi</em>Varr. RR 2.5.3

  • apēs, ut ajunt, dēbēmus imitārī

    we ought, as they say, to copy the beesSen. Ep. 84.3

  • tē in Ēpīrum salvum vēnisse et, ut scrībis, ex sententiā nāvigāsse vehementer gaudeō

    I am delighted that you reached Epirus safely and, according to your letter, had the voyage you wantedCic. Att. 5.21.1

See also according to, source.
